quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Tagrisso demonstrated unprecedented eight-year landmark (09-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Updated exploratory eight-year results from the ADAURA Phase III trial of adjuvant Tagrisso (osimertinib) in resected Stage IB-IIIA EGFR-mutated NSCLC, presented at WCLC 2026 and published in the Journal of Thoracic Oncology: Tagrisso reduced the risk of death versus placebo by 47% in the primary Stage II-IIIA population (HR 0.53; 95% CI 0.38-0.75) and by 48% in the overall population (HR 0.52; 95% CI 0.39-0.71); an estimated 74% of Tagrisso patients were alive at eight years versus 58% on placebo in the primary population, and 79% versus 64% in the overall population (682 patients; data cut-off 4 May 2026). Real-world evidence presented at the same meeting showed that early discontinuation of Tagrisso before completing the three-year course more than doubled the risk of recurrence or death, and FLAURA2 analyses (median follow-up 42.6 months) showed safety of Tagrisso plus platinum-pemetrexed consistent with established profiles. The company calls it the longest survival data reported in a global Phase III trial in this setting (company claim).
